# Q.3 a) STAT 4 C03

```{r}
# salary data loading
df = read.csv("Salary.csv")
head(df)
```

```{r}
cols = c("red", "green", "blue")
syms = c(1, 17)
plot(Salary~Exp, data=df, col=cols[Educ], pch=syms[Manage + 1])
```
# Q.3 b)

```{r}
model.b = lm(Salary~Exp * Educ * Manage, data=df)
summary((model.b))
```
The equations of the line has this form: Y = a + bX where a and b takes the following values
(Educ = 1, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + Educ
b = Exp + Exp:Educ

(Educ = 1, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + Educ + Manage + Educ:Manage
b = Exp + Exp:Educ + Exp:Manage + Exp:Educ:Manage

(Educ = 2, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + 2Educ
b = Exp + 2Exp:Educ

(Educ = 2, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + 2Educ + Manage + 2Educ:Manage
b = Exp + 2Exp:Educ + Exp:Manage + 2Exp:Educ:Manage

(Educ = 3, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + 3Educ
b = Exp + 3Exp:Educ

(Educ = 3, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + 3Educ + Manage + 3Educ:Manage
b = Exp + 3Exp:Educ + Exp:Manage + 3Exp:Educ:Manage

```{r}
b_Intercept = coef(model.b)["(Intercept)"]
b_Exp = coef(model.b)["Exp"]
b_Educ = coef(model.b)["Educ"]
b_Manage = coef(model.b)["Manage"]
b_Exp.Educ = coef(model.b)["Exp:Educ"]
b_Exp.Manage = coef(model.b)["Exp:Manage"]
b_Educ.Manage = coef(model.b)["Educ:Manage"]
b_All = coef(model.b)["Exp:Educ:Manage"]

plot(Salary ~ Exp, data = df, col = cols[Educ], pch = syms[Manage + 1])

abline(a = b_Intercept + b_Educ,
       b = b_Exp + b_Exp.Educ,
       col = "red", lwd = 2)        # Educ = 1, Manage = 0

abline(a = b_Intercept + b_Educ + b_Manage + b_Educ.Manage,
       b = b_Exp + b_Exp.Educ + b_Exp.Manage + b_All,
       col = "blue", lwd = 2)       # Educ = 1, Manage = 1

abline(a = b_Intercept + 2*b_Educ,
       b = b_Exp + 2*b_Exp.Educ,
       col = "green", lwd = 2)      # Educ = 2, Manage = 0

abline(a = b_Intercept + 2*b_Educ + b_Manage + 2*b_Educ.Manage,
       b = b_Exp + 2*b_Exp.Educ + b_Exp.Manage + 2*b_All,
       col = "yellow", lwd = 2)     # Educ = 2, Manage = 1

abline(a = b_Intercept + 3*b_Educ,
       b = b_Exp + 3*b_Exp.Educ,
       col = "black", lwd = 2)       # Educ = 3, Manage = 0

abline(a = b_Intercept + 3*b_Educ + b_Manage + 3*b_Educ.Manage,
       b = b_Exp + 3*b_Exp.Educ + b_Exp.Manage + 3*b_All,
       col = "orange", lwd = 2)     # Educ = 3, Manage = 1
```
# Q.3 c)

```{r}
model.r = lm(Salary~Exp+Educ*Manage, data=df)
summary(model.r)
```
The six lines are given by the following slope and intercept

(Educ = 1, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + Educ
b = Exp

(Educ = 1, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + Educ + Manage + Educ:Manage
b = Exp

(Educ = 2, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + 2·Educ
b = Exp

(Educ = 2, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + 2·Educ + Manage + 2·Educ:Manage
b = Exp

(Educ = 3, Manage = 0)
a = Intercept + 3·Educ
b = Exp

(Educ = 3, Manage = 1)
a = Intercept + 3·Educ + Manage + 3·Educ:Manage
b = Exp

# Q.3 d)

```{r}
anova(model.r, model.b)
```
The null hypotesis H0 assumes that the following coefficient are null:
Exp:Educ = Exp:Manage = Exp:Educ:Manage = 0
We have a p-value of 0.04 < 0.05 conclusion: H0 is rejected and The true relation doesn't have 6 parallel lines.
